title: Blog 1
content:
BUILDING AN AI AGENT WITH LONG-TERM MEMORY AND SANDBOX CODE EXECUTION USING AMAZON BEDROCK AGENTCORE When exploring AI Agents, I realized that a truly useful AI assistant requires more than just answering questions—it needs to remember information from past interactions and execute code to solve complex tasks.
For example, a data analysis AI Agent needs to remember how the user wants reports presented, while also having the capability to run Python to calculate metrics and generate charts instead of merely predicting results.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides components to build such systems without having to provision and manage the entire infrastructure from scratch.
1. OVERVIEW OF AMAZON BEDROCK AGENTCORE Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory: Supports storing and retrieving information across sessions, helping the Agent maintain context and remember useful details.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter: Provides an isolated code execution environment, allowing the Agent to run Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript to process data and perform calculations.
The key point is that Memory and Code Interpreter serve two distinct purposes. Memory preserves information needed for future use, while Code Interpreter executes code within a sandbox session.
2. SYSTEM ARCHITECTURE DESIGN Let’s design an AI Data Assistant capable of analyzing CSV files and remembering the user’s workflow.
Components used:
Amazon Bedrock: Provides the language model to understand requests and orchestrate tasks. AgentCore Memory: Stores and retrieves preferences and analysis rules. AgentCore Code Interpreter: Executes code to compute metrics and generate charts. Strands Agents SDK: Assists in building the Agent and integrating tools. Workflow:
User submits a data analysis request. Agent queries memory for relevant rules. Model creates an appropriate plan and code. Code Interpreter executes code inside the sandbox. Agent uses actual results to compose the report. Useful insights are saved to Memory for subsequent sessions. 3. IMPLEMENTING LONG-TERM MEMORY Not all conversation history needs to be stored long term. The Agent should prioritize information that adds value to upcoming interactions.
For example:
User prefers receiving reports in Markdown format. When analyzing data, missing values must be checked prior to calculation. Reports should include mean, median, and distribution charts. Upon receiving a new request, the Agent retrieves related information and injects it into the execution context.
4. CODE EXECUTION WITH CODE INTERPRETER LLMs can generate code but cannot guarantee it is always correct or secure. Executing AI-generated code directly on application servers poses risks to data, resources, and access privileges.
AgentCore Code Interpreter provides an isolated execution environment, separating code execution from the main application.
For example, when a user requests an analysis of scores.csv, the Agent can:
Read and inspect data. Handle missing or invalid values. Calculate mean and median. Generate distribution charts. Return results to the Agent to synthesize into a report. The sandbox can maintain session state during its lifecycle. However, temporary files or variables within the sandbox should not be considered permanent storage. If files need to be reused in future sessions, the application should persist them to appropriate storage such as Amazon S3.
5. REAL-WORLD SCENARIO ILLUSTRATION Suppose in the first session, the user asks to analyze exam score data and generate a Markdown report.
Upon completion, the Agent saves the report formatting preference to AgentCore Memory.
In the next session, the user simply uploads a new file and asks: “Analyze this file like last time.”
The Agent retrieves the saved memory, uses Code Interpreter to process the data, and produces the report following the stored rules without the user needing to repeat the full instructions.
This is the true value of combining long-term memory with tool execution: the Agent maintains operational context and performs tasks based on real computational results.
6. SECURITY AND COST When deploying in production environments, several considerations should be kept in mind:
Permissions: Users should only access memory and data within their authorized scope. Code security: Limit compute resources, file access permissions, and sandbox network connectivity. Memory management: Avoid storing unnecessary sensitive data; maintain appropriate update and deletion mechanisms. Monitoring: Track execution errors, response times, and resource utilization. Costs should also be evaluated comprehensively, including Amazon Bedrock, AgentCore Memory, Code Interpreter, and associated storage or monitoring services. Actual costs depend on usage patterns and current AWS pricing.
7. CONCLUSION Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory and Code Interpreter address two essential requirements when building AI Agents: retaining information across sessions and executing code in an isolated environment.
Combined with Amazon Bedrock and a framework like Strands Agents SDK, one can build applications such as an AI Data Analyst, Coding Assistant, or Research Assistant without having to build custom memory and runtime mechanisms from scratch.
References Amazon Bedrock AgentCore: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/ AgentCore Memory: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/long-term-memory-long-term.html AgentCore Code Interpreter: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/code-interpreter-getting-started.html Strands Agents: https://strandsagents.com/ #AWS #AmazonBedrock #BedrockAgentCore #AIAgent #GenerativeAI #AWSStudyGroup #CodeInterpreter #LongTermMemory

title: Event 1
content:
EVENT SUMMARY: FIRST CLOUD AI JOURNEY MEET UP Event Objectives Learn directly from experienced Tech Leads and enterprise engineers regarding Cloud and AI Agents in enterprise environments. Explore practical use cases: low-latency Vietnamese Voice AI, secure multi-account resource sharing in AWS Organizations, automated infrastructure pentesting via Security Agents, and cost optimization using MicroVMs on EC2 Spot. Expand professional networking with the AWS engineer community and fellow interns in the First Cloud AI Journey program. Speakers List Kiet Tran - Revve AI Long Huynh - Styl Solution Thinh Nguyen - Styl Solution Xuan An - Leader, AWS Student Builder Group HCMUTE Khoa Kieu - Tech Lead, ACB Nghi Danh - AWS Community Builder Key Highlights Session 1: Hear, Think, Speak - Building a Vietnamese voice-AI contact center on AWS Speaker: Kiet Tran (Revve AI) Explored Voice AI architecture aimed at reducing latency down to ~1.8s for smooth, natural voice conversations. Live demonstration of an AI system initiating outbound phone calls to interview Cloud Engineer candidates in Vietnamese with natural intonation and instant interactions. Session 2: AWS Resource Access Manager Speaker: Long Huynh (Styl Solution) Secure resource sharing strategies across accounts within AWS Organizations. Architectural approach for cost reduction, centralized network management, and tighter synergy between IAM policies and Service Control Policies (SCPs) to establish strict permission boundaries. Session 3: AWS Pentest with AWS Continuum / Security Agent Speaker: Thinh Nguyen (Styl Solution) Early-stage infrastructure security evaluation: reviewing Terraform code and integrating directly into GitLab/GitHub PRs to catch flaws. Simulating real attacker behavior with Security Agents to perform automated pentesting on SIT/UAT environments before actual deployment. Session 4: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Speaker: Xuan An (Leader, AWS Student Builder Group HCMUTE) Comprehensive overview of two foundational pillars for taking AI Agents to production: Agent Runtime: Running MicroVMs on EC2 Spot instances for significant cost savings. Memory System: Layered memory architecture with synchronous Short-term memory and asynchronous Long-term memory to deeply retain user context. Session 5: Kiro Crew Speakers: Khoa Kieu (Tech Lead, ACB) & Nghi Danh (AWS Community Builder) Running autonomous AI Agents 24/7 to support code reviews and continuous system health checks. Artifact Generation: AI Agent scrapes real-time recruitment data and renders visual statistical charts directly inside the conversation thread. Context Window Governance: Auto Compact mechanism triggered when context utilization reaches 70% - 90%, paired with Break down context functionality to analyze token consumption per component. Memory Management & Guardrails: Routine eviction of stale memories to prevent cost runaway, alongside strict security guardrails preventing AI from modifying infrastructure or exposing server secrets. Experience at the Event Attending the First Cloud AI Journey meet up at Bitexco was a deeply rewarding experience:
Open learning environment: Directly engaged with real-world challenges and technical solutions deployed at financial institutions and technology enterprises such as ACB, Styl Solution, and Revve AI. Engaging technical discussions: The closing Q&A session addressed technical nuances regarding context management, memory lifecycles, and enterprise guardrails in large-scale systems. Professional networking: Connected with seasoned industry leaders, alumni interns, and peers with similar career aspirations. Results Achieved Gained a holistic view of deploying production AI Agents and cloud infrastructure in enterprise settings. Deepened understanding of context window management, layered memory design (Short-term/Long-term), and security guardrail enforcement. Acquired knowledge on secure multi-account governance via AWS RAM and SCPs, alongside shift-left automated security pipelines in CI/CD. Mastered practical techniques to optimize operational costs for 24/7 AI workloads using MicroVMs on EC2 Spot instances. Lessons Learned Production-First Mindset: The gap between a Proof of Concept (PoC) and a production-grade system is substantial, requiring rigorous attention to real-time latency, operating costs, and stringent security boundaries. Cost Optimization Strategy: High-end instances are not always necessary; orchestrating EC2 Spot instances, MicroVMs, and routine memory hygiene significantly minimizes costs while maintaining reliability. Security by Design: Always enforce least-privilege principles and integrate automated security checks early into the CI/CD development pipeline (Shift-left security) to remediate vulnerabilities at the Pull Request stage. Active Networking & Continuous Learning: Participating in community events and engaging with experienced practitioners broadens technical perspectives, accelerates technology adoption, and provides clearer career guidance. title: Blog 2
content:
AMAZON TEXTRACT – BEYOND BASIC DOCUMENT TEXT EXTRACTION During the development of a recruitment system project, finding a solution to extract text from PDF documents was an essential requirement. When researching traditional OCR tools, I noticed that text recognition could face significant limitations, especially with documents having complex layouts, tables, or inconsistent formatting. In several evaluated cases, accuracy only ranged around 70–80%, depending on the tool and input document.
From that need, I learned about Amazon Textract – an AWS Machine Learning service that automatically extracts text and analyzes document structure.
What caught my attention was not just the character recognition capability, but how Textract transforms document content into structured data for downstream application processing.
1. CONTEXT AND LIMITATIONS OF TRADITIONAL OCR Traditional OCR tools approach documents by scanning images and attempting to recognize individual characters line by line. This approach exhibits clear limitations:
Multi-column documents: Reading order is easily scrambled across columns, altering the original meaning of paragraphs. Form-based data: Difficult to distinguish between field labels and the values submitted by users. Tabular data: Flattened into continuous text strings, losing relationships between rows and columns. Variable layouts: Real-world documents rarely follow a fixed template, causing rigid coordinate-based methods to struggle. To solve this challenge, Amazon Textract provides an automated approach to document structure analysis without requiring a custom end-to-end preprocessing pipeline.
2. OVERVIEW OF AMAZON TEXTRACT Amazon Textract is an AWS Machine Learning service developed to read and comprehend documents similarly to human inspection.
Unlike basic OCR that only returns raw text strings, Textract analyzes the spatial architecture of documents and returns detailed information on every component: pages, lines, words, key-value pairs, tables, and individual cells. Each element includes its spatial position on the page along with a confidence score for the recognition result.
3. KEY FEATURES OF AMAZON TEXTRACT Textract provides multiple useful features catering to diverse document processing needs:
Text Detection: Detects printed text and handwriting in supported documents and images. The output contains both textual content and spatial location on the page. This capability fits applications needing to digitize documents for search, archiving, or downstream processing. Form Extraction: A notable capability of Textract is recognizing relationships between field labels and corresponding values, also known as key-value pairs. For example, from a form containing Name: Nguyen Van A, the system identifies Name as the field label and Nguyen Van A as the corresponding value, rather than returning a continuous string. Table Extraction: Capable of recognizing tables, rows, columns, and cell contents. As a result, structured data within documents is converted into convenient formats for downstream workflows. This feature is particularly helpful when processing reports, invoices, data sheets, and table-heavy documents. Queries: One of the most compelling capabilities. Instead of requesting the system to parse the entire document, Queries allows specifying target information using natural language questions. For example, on a suitable document, the application can ask questions such as: What is the customer name? What is the invoice date? What is the total amount? Textract locates the corresponding information and returns separate results for each query. This helps applications focus directly on needed data without manual post-filtering. Layout and Signature Detection: Layout: Recognizes structural elements such as titles, paragraphs, lists, tables, and page numbers, preserving document layout information. Signature Detection: Detects signature locations in documents and returns coordinates along with confidence scores. These capabilities expand Textract usage in document verification, profile review, and workflow automation. 4. NOTABLE APIS Amazon Textract provides several APIs for different requirements:
DetectDocumentText: General text recognition. AnalyzeDocument: Analyzes text, forms, tables, layouts, and queries. AnalyzeExpense: Extracts data related to invoices and receipts. AnalyzeID: Extracts information from supported identity documents. Analyze Lending: Classifies and analyzes loan document packages according to service workflows. Depending on the use case, applications can choose synchronous processing for quick responses or asynchronous processing for multi-page documents and large workloads.
5. PRODUCTION CONSIDERATIONS Despite its powerful capabilities, Textract does not mean every document is recognized with absolute perfection. Results depend on document quality, language, layout, and target information type.
A useful feature is that Textract returns confidence scores for recognition results, allowing applications to establish validation rules or request manual verification when necessary. However, confidence scores should not be treated as an absolute guarantee of accuracy.
Additionally, applications need to select the appropriate API, verify supported languages and document types, and plan for processing volume costs.
6. CONCLUSION Exploring Amazon Textract during project development broadened my perspective on applying AI and Machine Learning to document processing.
Textract goes beyond OCR by supporting structural recognition, extracting form and table data, answering natural language queries, and handling specialized document types.
This is a valuable service to consider when building applications that automate document reading and processing, especially when integrating these capabilities via managed APIs rather than building a custom recognition pipeline from scratch.
References Amazon Textract Features: https://aws.amazon.com/textract/features/ Amazon Textract Developer Guide: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/ Analyzing Documents: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/how-it-works-analyzing.html #AWS #AmazonTextract #OCR #MachineLearning #AI #DocumentProcessing #AWSStudyGroup

title: Event 2
content:
EVENT SUMMARY: FIRST CLOUD AI JOURNEY - COMMUNITY DAY Organized Date & Time: 09:00 - 12:00, October 31, 2026 Location: 26th Floor, Bitexco Financial Tower, 02 Hai Trieu, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City Role: Attendee Event Objectives Discover structured self-study methodologies, certification paths, and interactive learning through AWS Cloud Quest. Learn engineering mindsets for integrating AI into automated Pull Request reviews and End-to-End (E2E) testing pipelines. Gain real-world insights from a serverless Multiplayer Web Game project using Lambda, DynamoDB, SQS, and EventBridge, addressing challenges like Cold Starts. Explore Lambda Web Functions paired with CloudFront Origin Access Control (OAC) to eliminate API Gateway latency and optimize cloud spending. Understand resilient asynchronous architecture patterns using Amazon SQS, Long Polling, and Dead Letter Queues (DLQ). Acquire practical strategies and communication etiquette for contributing to large open-source projects. Speakers List Minh Tuấn - Cloud Enthusiast & Certified Builder Henry Đức Bùi - Head of Engineering at Cloud Tinker Phúc Khang - Former Intern at First Cloud Journey Thịnh Nguyễn - Dev Cloud Engineer at Styl Solution Cẩm Đào - Software & Cloud Engineer Hùng Trần - Senior Engineer at NAP Detailed Session Summaries Session 1: Effective AWS Learning Pathways Speaker: Minh Tuấn Summary: Shared practical approaches to building a personalized AWS learning path from scratch toward professional certifications such as Solutions Architect and Developer. Guided attendees on making the most of AWS Skill Builder resources, combining architectural blueprints with hands-on practice. Introduced gamified learning through AWS Cloud Quest, where learners take on the role of a city engineer to resolve real infrastructure issues, reinforcing concepts much better than rote memorization. Emphasized doing hands-on labs to build troubleshooting intuition, which is essential for tackling scenario-based exam questions. Session 2: Accelerating Software Development with AI Speaker: Henry Đức Bùi (Head of Engineering at Cloud Tinker) Summary: Discussed reshaping engineering mindsets in the AI era, treating AI as a capable pair programmer rather than a human replacement. Applied large language models to automate code reviews: integrating bots into GitHub/GitLab Pull Requests to spot syntax errors, flag security risks early, and suggest optimizations. Built automated End-to-End (E2E) testing pipelines by generating realistic user-flow test cases with AI, catching regressions on CI/CD before deploying to staging. Focused on team efficiency: freeing engineers from repetitive manual checks so they can concentrate on architectural design and core business logic. Session 3: 3 Months Internship Journey at First Cloud Journey Speaker: Phúc Khang Summary: Reflected on the 3-month internship graduation project: building a real-time Multiplayer Web Game running entirely on a Serverless stack. Architecture overview: AWS Lambda and WebSocket APIs manage persistent bidirectional connections between players and game lobbies. Amazon DynamoDB stores live game states, player profiles, and leaderboards with millisecond response times. Amazon SQS and EventBridge queue player interactions and handle game notifications asynchronously. Lessons learned: Managing computing expenses during unexpected player surges. Reducing Lambda cold start latency through Provisioned Concurrency and trimmed deployment bundles. Adopting an event-driven mindset: keeping services decoupled and modular with built-in error handling. Session 4: AWS Lambda Web Function Speaker: Thịnh Nguyễn (Dev Cloud Engineer at Styl Solution) Summary: Analyzed bottlenecks in traditional Lambda and API Gateway pairings: high request-based costs at scale, multi-hop network latency, and the 29-second timeout ceiling. Introduced Lambda Web Adapter / Lambda Function URLs routed directly through Amazon CloudFront: Run standard web frameworks (Express.js, FastAPI, Go Gin) on Lambda without rewriting code for API Gateway event formats. Secure the Function URL using Origin Access Control (OAC), ensuring only authorized traffic through the CDN can invoke the function. Add AWS WAF at the edge, eliminate API Gateway charges entirely, reduce network latency, and extend maximum execution time up to 15 minutes. Session 5: Building Asynchronous Systems with Amazon SQS Speaker: Cẩm Đào Summary: Discussed shifting from synchronous request-response models to asynchronous event queues to ease database pressure and improve response times for users. Utilized Amazon SQS as an elastic buffer to decouple frontend ingestion from heavy background processing. Compared Short Polling with Long Polling, demonstrating how Long Polling reduces empty API calls, lowers querying costs, and speeds up message retrieval. Configured Dead Letter Queues (DLQ) with a defined retry policy (maxReceiveCount) to isolate failed messages, allowing engineering teams to inspect errors without interrupting main workflows. Session 6: Practical Guide to Open Source Contributions Speaker: Hùng Trần (Senior Engineer at NAP) Summary: Demystified open-source participation: newcomers do not need to be veteran experts or read entire massive codebases to start contributing. Practical roadmap: Start by looking for issues tagged good first issue, documentation, or bug-reproduce in popular repositories like Kubernetes, AWS SDKs, or Terraform. Learn how to write clear issue descriptions, provide reproducible test cases, and submit structured Pull Requests. Maintain polite and constructive communication, respecting maintainers’ review capacity. Cultivate patience: taking rigorous code review feedback as a valuable learning opportunity to sharpen coding standards and build a credible public portfolio. Event Experience Attending in person at the AWS Vietnam office (Bitexco Financial Tower) provided an engaging atmosphere with open discussions alongside seasoned engineers. The presentations struck a great balance between high-level guidance and concrete technical details, transparently analyzing trade-offs in operational costs and performance. Hearing real stories from the former intern’s project and the open-source session provided strong encouragement to build personal projects and actively participate in technical communities. Key Outcomes Gained clear guidance on structuring self-study and certification goals using interactive AWS tools. Understood how to adopt Lambda Web Functions and CloudFront OAC to reduce costs and latency for serverless web applications. Mastered asynchronous system design with Amazon SQS, Long Polling, and error isolation via Dead Letter Queues. Learned how to apply AI tools effectively for automated code reviews and test generation on CI/CD pipelines. Felt more confident about taking the first steps toward contributing to global open-source projects. Lessons Learned Understanding service billing models and architecture boundaries enables much more cost-effective solutions than relying on default configurations. Designing with an async-first mindset is essential for maintaining stability and preventing bottlenecks in high-scale systems. The most effective learning always comes from getting hands-on: building real projects, troubleshooting unexpected errors, and sharing solutions with the community. title: Proposal
content:
Project: Cloud Job — Cloud Recruitment Platform Powered by Automated AI Resume Screening Cloud Job is a dedicated recruitment web platform specializing in Cloud Computing careers (Cloud Computing, DevOps, Solutions Architect, SysOps), featuring an end-to-end automated AI screening pipeline powered by AWS Serverless & Generative AI.
1. Problem Overview Driven by the rapid expansion of Cloud Computing, demand for high-caliber infrastructure talents—such as Cloud Engineers, DevOps specialists, SysOps administrators, and Solutions Architects—has grown exponentially. However, cloud roles demand strict technical criteria covering cloud service proficiencies (AWS, Containers, CI/CD, IaC) and formal certifications. When screening applications, enterprises face significant hurdles:
Applications arrive in large volumes yet remain fragmented across email threads and generic submission forms. Technical leads and recruiters must manually open and scrutinize each PDF document to assess complex cloud skill sets, project histories, and certification validity. This process consumes dozens of hours every week, creating hiring bottlenecks, delayed candidate communications, and potential talent loss due to reviewer fatigue or cognitive bias. Proposed Approach: Construct Cloud Job — an intelligent recruitment portal dedicated to the cloud employment market, architected on AWS Serverless and Generative AI:
Web Portal Interface: Provides an intuitive experience for two key user personas: Technology Recruiters managing job listings and candidate pipelines; Cloud Candidates discovering specialized roles and submitting applications online. Asynchronous Processing Pipeline: When a candidate submits a PDF resume, it uploads directly to secure Amazon S3 storage via short-lived Presigned URLs, subsequently triggering an asynchronous processing chain via Amazon SQS to guarantee high availability without system bottlenecks. AI Evaluation Pipeline: Amazon Textract: Automatically extracts raw text content from multi-page PDF resumes. Amazon Bedrock: Leverages the Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 Large Language Model to evaluate resume contents against specific Job Description criteria. The model systematically compares cloud skills, project experiences, and AWS certifications, outputting quantitative scores, strength/gap assessments, and structured JSON summaries. Automated Notifications: Integrates Amazon SES to deliver automated confirmation emails to applicants and enable one-click interview invitations for recruiters. Cost & Operational Optimization: Operates entirely on a Serverless pay-as-you-go model with zero idle compute costs. 2. Objectives & Scope Concrete Objectives Automate Preliminary Screening: Reduce resume parsing and scoring latency from several minutes down to under 60 seconds, eliminating 80–90% of manual reading overhead. Enhance Objectivity and Consistency: Enforce standardized evaluation criteria across all applications against job requirements, minimizing human bias. Modern Candidate & Recruiter Experience: Provide intuitive dashboards, candidate score rankings with detailed evaluations, and real-time state updates delivered via WebSocket Push. Embody Cloud Architecture Best Practices: Deliver the comprehensive Cloud Job platform combining over 10 AWS services strictly aligned with all 6 pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework: Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Operational Excellence, and Sustainability. Implementation Scope MVP Scope (Core Deliverables): Authentication & RBAC: User management through Amazon Cognito with 3 distinct roles (Candidate, Recruiter, Admin) and Company Profile support for collaborative HR workflows. Job Management & Applications: Recruiters publish, edit, and close job postings; Candidates search vacancies, manage profile information, and maintain default resumes. Standardized PDF Intake: Exclusively supports PDF format up to 5MB uploaded directly to Amazon S3 via secure Presigned URLs; duplicate submission protection and application withdrawal mechanisms; dual lifecycle tracking for recruitment status and asynchronous AI processing status. Objective AI Pipeline: Asynchronous processing orchestrated by Amazon SQS and AWS Lambda Workers; text extraction via Amazon Textract; automatic personal identification data filtering before invoking Amazon Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5 for rubric-based scoring into structured JSON outputs. Human-in-the-Loop Review: 3-column side-by-side comparison interface; internal recruiter notes, star ratings, status progression with an immutable audit trail; controlled re-scoring capabilities. Talent Pool & Analytics: Candidate skill gap analytics; searchable talent repository with automated re-discovery recommendations for new job postings. Data Privacy & Operations: Purpose-based consent tracking and DSR anonymization workflows; verified zero model training policy on Bedrock; automated email delivery via Amazon SES; centralized logs, metric dashboards, and alarms through Amazon CloudWatch; automated infrastructure clean-up routines. Extended Scope (Post-MVP): Candidate job bookmarking. Automated job notification subscriptions via email. Multi-dimensional filtering for compensation ranges and remote/hybrid modes. AWS WAF integration for edge protection on CloudFront and API Gateway. 3. Problems to Solve Challenges and Limitations in Current Processes Process Bottlenecks: Typical hiring campaigns receive 100 to 300 resumes per opening. Manual reading, sorting, and documentation consume 15 to 25 hours per vacancy. Slow Turnaround Times: Candidates wait 1 to 3 weeks for preliminary feedback, risking dropouts to competing employers. Lack of Standardization: Unstructured evaluations and dispersed notes make objective comparisons across applicant cohorts difficult. Prohibitive SaaS ATS Pricing: Commercial recruitment tools demand costly monthly subscriptions ranging from $100 to $500, creating unnecessary expenses for smaller departments or short-term hiring drives. Practical Efficiency and Cost Optimization Strategy Time Savings: Reduces initial resume screening time by over 80%. Hiring managers focus immediate attention on pre-qualified candidate shortlists. Ultra-Low Infrastructure Costs: Leveraging serverless architectures results in operational costs of approximately $1.00 – $2.00 USD / month for testing and ~$28.08 USD / month when processing 2,000 resumes. Rapid Payback Period: Achieves positive ROI within the initial operational month by saving dozens of skilled engineering and recruiter working hours. 4. Preliminary Solution Architecture Overall Cloud Job Pure Serverless Architecture on AWS (Multi-AZ Managed Services — Zero-VPC / Pay-Per-Use)
The solution implements a 100% Pure Serverless layered architecture, fully decoupling low-latency synchronous API operations from background AI orchestration powered by EventBridge Pipes and Step Functions Claim-Check patterns:
Official AWS Service Catalog AWS Service Category Technical Role in System Architecture AWS WAF Edge Security Protects perimeter traffic against SQL Injection, XSS, HTTP Floods, malicious bots, and request rate abuse via Global WebACLs associated with CloudFront. Amazon CloudFront Global Edge CDN Unified Edge Ingress distributing Amplify React SPA assets, routing REST API traffic, and upgrading WebSocket handshakes using TLS 1.3. AWS Amplify Hosting Frontend Hosting Hosts frontend assets with continuous integration and automated deployment pipelines connected directly to GitHub. Amazon Cognito Identity Management Manages user registration, sign-in, and Role-Based Access Control (Candidate, Recruiter, Admin) along with custom enterprise attributes. Amazon API Gateway API Gateway REST API secured with Resource Policies and Cognito JWT Authorizers; WebSocket API delivers live scoring results back to clients, eliminating HTTP polling. AWS Lambda Serverless Compute Executes backend business logic: authorization verification, Presigned URL generation, idempotency validation, PII redaction, and JSON validation on Node.js TypeScript. Amazon S3 Object Storage Quarantines uploaded PDF resumes up to 5MB, partitions storage by verification state, and provides secure direct upload capabilities via 5-minute Presigned URLs. Amazon GuardDuty Threat Detection Automatically scans uploaded resumes with Malware Protection for S3 before permitting downstream processing. Amazon SQS Message Queue Buffers bursts and isolates traffic spikes, verifying idempotency keys (document_id) before initiating Step Functions workflows. Amazon SQS Dead-Letter Queue Error Isolation Quarantines unrecoverable execution failures after 3 retry attempts to preserve data and support root cause investigation. Amazon EventBridge Event Routing Filters GuardDuty malware scan outcomes and routes clean upload notifications to downstream consumers. Amazon EventBridge Pipes Event Integration Connects Amazon SQS queues directly to AWS Step Functions with automated payload filtering and transformation. AWS Step Functions Workflow Orchestrator Sequentially coordinates: Amazon Textract $\to$ PII Redaction $\to$ Amazon Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5 scoring, complete with exponential backoff retries. Amazon Textract AI Document OCR Reads PDF files directly from S3, providing asynchronous document parsing for multi-page resumes without keeping network connections open. Amazon Bedrock Runtime Generative AI Executes Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 to transform unstructured resumes into validated JSON schemas based on a standardized 100-point rubric. Amazon A2I Human-in-the-Loop Serves as an automated fallback when OCR confidence scores drop below 80% or output formatting fails, routing resumes into human review queues. Amazon DynamoDB NoSQL Database Single-Table On-Demand database with sub-10ms response times, persisting structured resume JSON records, idempotency locks, and candidate rankings. Amazon SES Email Communication Dispatches automated submission acknowledgments, screening completion summaries, and interview invitation emails. Amazon CloudWatch Observability Aggregates structured logs, monitors operational metrics in real-time, and triggers alerts on DLQ backlogs or threshold breaches. AWS KMS Data Encryption Manages Customer Managed Keys (CMK) to ensure cryptographic envelope encryption for data at rest in Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB. 4 Key Technical Differentiators Automated Quarantine & Malware Screening: Restricts client uploads to temporary server-generated Presigned URLs; all incoming files land inside an isolated S3 quarantine bucket and undergo automatic malware inspection via Amazon GuardDuty. Sequential Step Functions Orchestration with A2I Fallback: Utilizes Claim-Check patterns to prevent payload overflows; coordinates Textract OCR and Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5 evaluation, automatically redirecting anomalous outputs to human reviewers via Amazon A2I. Event Idempotency & Real-Time WebSocket Push: Idempotency locks based on document identifiers prevent duplicate processing expenses during repeated S3 upload events; scoring results push immediately to client viewports over WebSockets. Pure Serverless Zero-Cost Network: Completely eliminates fixed monthly expenses associated with VPCs, NAT Gateways, and PrivateLink endpoints; relies on IAM Zero-Trust and TLS 1.3 over the AWS Global Backbone with $0.00/month idle networking charges. 5. Implementation Plan & Timeline The 9-week development roadmap spans from October 27, 2026 to December 31, 2026, advancing through 7 synchronized phases balancing infrastructure-as-code and frontend interfaces across defined milestones:
Phase Timeframe AWS Service Configuration Focus Frontend Development & Control Milestones Phase 0
Analysis & Design Oct 27 – Oct 31 Technical requirements specification, Serverless architecture sign-off, DynamoDB schema, API design, 100-point rubric, and AWS Pricing Calculator estimates. Milestone M0 (Oct 31): Completion of SRS documentation, architecture diagrams, API/DB specifications, and project proposal. Phase 1
Foundations & Auth Nov 01 – Nov 08 AWS CDK/SAM initialization; Cognito user pool with 3 role groups, S3 Quarantine, SQS queues, CloudFront distribution, AWS WAF, and Amplify Hosting. Delineate React Vite scaffolding; complete public Job Board and authentication login/register views.
Milestone M1 (Nov 08): Cloud networking, authentication, and core application shell operational. Phase 2
Core Business & S3 Intake Nov 09 – Nov 22 API Gateway REST endpoints and Lambda business handlers for company profiles, job listings, and Presigned URLs; S3 Quarantine, GuardDuty integration, and SQS idempotency. Candidate workflows: Direct PDF uploads to S3 Quarantine, dual-status application tracking, and application withdrawal; recruiter vacancy management.
Milestone M2 (Nov 22): Job posting, quarantine uploads, and queueing pipelines operational. Phase 3
AI Step Functions & A2I Nov 23 – Dec 06 Step Functions orchestration: Textract OCR $\to$ PII sanitization $\to$ Bedrock Claude Haiku 4.5 rubric scoring; retry policies and Amazon A2I fallback routing. Recruiter workflows: Candidate leaderboard, 3-column side-by-side review with manual review fallback modes, and talent rediscovery.
Milestone M3 (Dec 06): Automated AI evaluation pipeline and recruiter review dashboard complete. Phase 4
WebSockets, SES & Admin Dec 07 – Dec 13 API Gateway WebSocket endpoints delivering sub-500ms push updates; Amazon SES email templates; DSR anonymization handlers, CloudWatch dashboards, and alarms. Frontend WebSocket integration; complete administrative dashboard, dead-letter queue monitoring, and data privacy compliance views.
Milestone M4 (Dec 13): Full integration of all AWS services and frontend interfaces complete. Phase 5
Testing & Feature Freeze Dec 14 – Dec 20 End-to-end integration testing: S3 Quarantine validation, idempotency controls, Step Functions retries, A2I fallbacks, WebSocket push, prompt injection defenses, and 50-resume load tests; cost audits. End-to-end UI regression testing across all screens; formal feature freeze and production v1.0.0 release tagging.
Milestone M5 (Dec 20): 100% test cases verified, solution demo-ready. Phase 6
Documentation & Final Handover Dec 21 – Dec 31 Author reproducible bilingual workshop lab guides; finalize automated one-click teardown scripts ensuring $0.00 residual cost upon stack deletion. Produce comprehensive video demonstration covering Step Functions execution graphs and live WebSocket push notifications; final submission compilation.
Milestone M6 (Dec 31): Project documentation and submission complete. 6. Budget & Cost Estimation (Cost Estimation) Cost forecasts were calculated independently and verified against the official AWS Pricing Calculator in the us-east-1 region across two operational tiers:
Scenario A (Demo / Workshop): 5 job openings, 100 PDF resumes/month (2 pages/resume average), 2,500 API requests, WAF disabled. Scenario B (Production SMB): 50 job openings, 2,000 PDF resumes/month (4,000 Textract pages, ~5M input / ~1.6M output tokens for Claude Haiku 4.5, 50,000 API requests), AWS WAF active. Monthly Cost Summary Table AWS Service Group Scenario A (Demo 100 CV) Scenario B (SMB 2,000 CV) Calculation Baseline & Free Tier Coverage AWS Lambda $0.00 $0.00 Fully covered under permanent Free Tier: 1M requests & 400,000 GB-s/month. Amazon API Gateway $0.01 $0.19 REST API ($3.50/1M reqs) plus WebSocket ($0.25/1M mins & $1.00/1M messages). Amazon CloudFront $0.00 $0.00 Covered under Free Tier: 1 TB data transfer out & 10M requests/month. AWS WAF $0.00 (Off) $0.03 Request inspection charges based on processed traffic. Amazon Cognito $0.00 $0.01 Permanent Free Tier covers up to 50,000 monthly active users. Amazon S3 $0.04 $0.23 Standard S3 storage with Lifecycle policies purging objects after 90 days. GuardDuty S3 Malware $0.11 $0.79 $0.20 per GB of scanned resume data. Amazon SQS $0.00 $0.02 Covered under Free Tier: 1M SQS requests/month. Amazon EventBridge Pipes $0.00 $0.02 Polling messages from SQS to Step Functions via Pipes. AWS Step Functions $0.00 $0.30 Demo covered by Free Tier 4,000 transitions; SMB incurs minimal transition fees. Amazon Textract $0.30 $6.00 DetectDocumentText rate: $1.50 per 1,000 processed PDF pages. Amazon Bedrock (Haiku 4.5) $11.70 $11.70 Claude Haiku 4.5 token pricing based on resume parsing and rubric scoring volume. Amazon DynamoDB $0.51 $1.25 On-Demand capacity leveraging 25GB of permanent free storage. Amazon SES $0.01 $0.30 Email confirmations and interview scheduling notices. AWS KMS $1.06 $1.15 1 Customer Managed Key protecting encryption at rest. Amazon CloudWatch $1.31 $2.82 Log ingestion retention plus standard alarm metrics. AWS Amplify Hosting $1.27 $2.87 Frontend build compute minutes and static client-side distribution. AWS Secrets Manager $0.40 $0.40 Secure configuration parameter storage. A2I, CloudTrail, IAM $0.00 $0.00 Incur zero additional charges under standard AWS usage terms. TOTAL MONTHLY COST $18.63 USD $28.08 USD 80% – 88% savings compared to traditional VPC deployments ($115 – $148/month) Unit Cost per Candidate Application: In the Production SMB tier (2,000 resumes/month), the comprehensive AWS cost to process an application end-to-end—including upload, malware scan, OCR extraction, AI rubric scoring, email dispatch, and WebSocket UI push—amounts to ~$0.014 USD (~350 VNĐ / resume). Compared to manual recruiter screening expenses ($0.60 – $1.20 USD per 5–10 minute review), the platform achieves over 98% direct screening cost reduction. Budgetary Safeguards: Configured AWS Budgets send email alerts at thresholds of $10 USD (Demo) and $35 USD/month (Production SMB), providing strict financial boundaries. 7. Risks & Mitigation Strategies Potential Risk Impact Probability Mitigation Strategy Contingency Plan Bedrock Model Access Pending in Selected Region High Medium Verify regional model availability and submit model access requests early in Phase 0; default to us-east-1 for comprehensive model support. Maintain prompt templates compatible with both Anthropic Claude and Amazon Titan models. Amazon SES Sandbox Constraints Medium High Pre-verify all test and demo recipient email addresses during Phase 1 setup. Document sandbox prerequisites clearly within lab guides; surface console log notifications when unverified addresses are encountered. Corrupted, Illegible, or Oversized Resumes Medium Medium Strictly enforce PDF format constraints and a 5MB maximum size limit; implement Lambda timeout and exception handlers; flag failed records with descriptive error logs. Route unrecoverable processing failures into Dead-Letter Queues for diagnostic inspection without disrupting concurrent queue processing. Prompt Injection Attacks via Resume Content Medium Low Design resilient prompt structures by strictly isolating resume data within XML delimiters such as <cv_content>; instruct models via system prompts to function strictly as objective evaluators. Execute adversarial injection test scenarios during Phase 5 testing to reinforce system prompts against jailbreak attempts. Unexpected Cloud Spending Spikes Medium Low Establish AWS Budget email alerts at $5 and $10 thresholds immediately; enforce S3 Lifecycle policies purging files after 30 to 90 days. Maintain automated single-command teardown scripts enabling operators to decommission all active infrastructure immediately following tests.

title: Blog 3
content:
AWS CODEBUILD COMBINED WITH CODEPIPELINE – EXPLORING HOW TO BUILD CI/CD PIPELINES ON AWS During software development, whenever source code changes occur, developers frequently have to perform repetitive manual tasks: installing dependencies, building the application, running test suites, and deploying new releases. When handled manually, this release process is not only time-consuming but also prone to human error.
While exploring AWS and DevOps solutions, I became interested in automating this workflow using CI/CD. Among AWS services supporting CI/CD, AWS CodeBuild and AWS CodePipeline can be effectively combined to build a comprehensive automation pipeline.
What is fascinating is that these two services serve distinct, complementary roles: CodePipeline orchestrates workflow stages, while CodeBuild executes concrete tasks such as building source code, executing tests, and packaging artifacts.
AWS CodePipeline – Orchestrating the Entire CI/CD Workflow CodePipeline is AWS’s fully managed CI/CD service designed to automate release pipeline stages. Instead of writing custom glue scripts to connect each phase, developers define a cohesive pipeline composed of Stages and Actions.
A typical pipeline generally contains three primary stages:
Source: Fetches source code from repositories such as GitHub or AWS CodeCommit. Build: Compiles the application, installs dependencies, and runs automated tests. Deploy: Delivers the updated application artifact to the target deployment environment. A key highlight of CodePipeline is its ability to seamlessly integrate various AWS services and external developer tools into a unified execution flow. When changes are pushed to the repository, the pipeline triggers automatically and executes stages in configured order.
Furthermore, CodePipeline provides real-time status tracking for each Stage and Action. If a step fails, you can immediately pinpoint the exact point of failure without manually debugging the entire release process.
AWS CodeBuild – Automating Build and Testing Workflows If CodePipeline acts as the coordinator, CodeBuild is the workhorse that performs the actual build and test execution.
AWS CodeBuild is a fully managed build service providing scalable compute environments on-demand, eliminating the need to provision, patch, and maintain dedicated build servers.
A core component when working with CodeBuild is the buildspec.yml file. This YAML configuration file defines commands and settings executed during each build phase.
A typical buildspec is structured into distinct phases:
install: Installs the required runtime environments and build dependencies. pre_build: Prepares the environment, configures runtime parameters, or logs in to container registries. build: Compiles source code, runs automated tests, or packages the application. post_build: Executes post-build operations such as pushing Docker images or generating output artifacts. This structure is highly intuitive because the entire build lifecycle is version-controlled directly alongside the source code. Modifying build steps merely requires updating the buildspec file rather than logging into build servers to reconfigure environments.
How Do CodeBuild and CodePipeline Work Together? To understand how these services cooperate, consider a standard application deployment scenario leveraging GitHub, AWS CodePipeline, CodeBuild, Amazon ECR, and Amazon ECS.
When a developer pushes commits to GitHub, CodePipeline detects the change and initiates a new execution. The Source Stage retrieves the corresponding commit revision and passes the output artifact to the Build Stage.
Here, CodeBuild executes instructions defined in buildspec.yml: installing dependencies, running unit tests, building the Docker image, and pushing it to Amazon ECR.
Once the build phase succeeds, the pipeline progresses to the Deploy Stage to update the service on Amazon ECS. In a standard ECS deployment workflow, CodePipeline consumes an imagedefinitions.json artifact to determine the newly deployed container image URI.
Crucially, if the Build Stage fails, the pipeline halts immediately, preventing unverified or broken changes from ever reaching production environments.
A Notable Concept: Artifacts in CodePipeline Understanding the concept of Artifacts is essential, as they represent the data exchange mechanism between pipeline stages.
An artifact is simply the input or output dataset of a pipeline Action. For instance, the Source Stage produces an artifact containing raw source code; the Build Stage receives this input, executes the build, and generates an output artifact containing imagedefinitions.json for consumption by the Deploy Stage.
Artifacts are securely persisted in an artifact store, typically backed by Amazon S3. This decoupling allows stages to operate independently while maintaining an integrated, reproducible pipeline.
Key Considerations for Real-World Implementations Constructing robust CI/CD pipelines involves several practical design considerations beyond connecting stages:
IAM Permissions: CodePipeline and CodeBuild require appropriate IAM roles to interact with source repositories, S3, ECR, and target infrastructure, adhering strictly to the Principle of Least Privilege. Secrets Management: Sensitive information such as API keys, database credentials, and tokens must never be hardcoded into source repositories or buildspec files. Instead, retrieve them dynamically from AWS Secrets Manager or Systems Manager Parameter Store. Monitoring & Observability: CodeBuild integrates natively with Amazon CloudWatch Logs to capture all build logs, simplifying troubleshooting for dependency failures, broken tests, or packaging errors. Build Optimization: Utilize CodeBuild caching mechanisms, select optimal compute types, and optimize Docker layer caching to reduce execution latency and minimize build costs. For containerized workloads, configuring the CodeBuild environment properly, granting ECR push permissions, and implementing traceable Docker image tagging strategies ensure reliable auditability back to the specific source commit.
Conclusion AWS CodeBuild and AWS CodePipeline are complementary services that form a powerful backbone for automated software delivery:
CodePipeline: Organizes, automates, and orchestrates CI/CD release stages. CodeBuild: Provides fully managed, isolated compute power to execute build and test tasks. When combined with Amazon ECR and Amazon ECS, teams can establish an automated, reliable pipeline spanning from initial code push all the way to production deployment.
References AWS CodePipeline: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/welcome.html AWS CodeBuild: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/welcome.html Buildspec Reference: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codebuild/latest/userguide/build-spec-ref.html CodeBuild Action in CodePipeline: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/action-reference-CodeBuild.html Deploying to Amazon ECS with CodePipeline: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/ecs-cd-pipeline.html #AWS #AWSCodeBuild #AWSCodePipeline #CICD #DevOps #AmazonECR #AmazonECS #CloudComputing #AWSStudyGroup

title: Blogs Posted
content:
Blog 1 - BUILDING AN AI AGENT WITH LONG-TERM MEMORY AND SANDBOX CODE EXECUTION USING AMAZON BEDROCK AGENTCORE This article introduces building an intelligent AI Data Assistant by combining Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Memory (long-term memory) and Code Interpreter (isolated sandbox code execution). This enables the Agent to maintain context and remember user preferences across sessions while executing Python code to calculate metrics and plot charts accurately instead of guessing results.
Blog 2 - AMAZON TEXTRACT – BEYOND BASIC DOCUMENT TEXT EXTRACTION This article explores Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) utilizing Amazon Textract within a recruitment system project. It highlights Textract’s advantages over conventional OCR, showcasing key-value pair form extraction, table structure preservation, natural language queries, signature detection, and considerations around confidence score thresholds and operational cost optimization.
Blog 3 - AWS CODEBUILD COMBINED WITH CODEPIPELINE – EXPLORING HOW TO BUILD CI/CD PIPELINES ON AWS This article explores how to build an automated CI/CD pipeline on AWS by combining AWS CodePipeline (workflow orchestration) and AWS CodeBuild (build and test execution). It covers buildspec.yml configuration, artifact exchange via Amazon S3, end-to-end integration with GitHub, Amazon ECR, and Amazon ECS, alongside key best practices for IAM least-privilege permissions, secrets management, and build performance optimization.
